original_question: Let L(d; m_1, ..., m_n) denote the linear system of plane curves of degree d passing through n points with multiplicities at least m_1, ..., m_n, and let L(d; m_1, ..., m_r, m_{r+1}, ..., m_n) denote the analogous system where the first r points are constrained to be collinear but are otherwise general. If d >= m_1 + ... + m_r, is it true that L(d; m_1, ..., m_n) is nonempty if and only if the corresponding system with the first r points collinear is nonempty?
target_in_paper: Problem 3.9.4 in Section 3.9 ("Imposing higher vanishing order at one point"), stated after the setup for L(d | m1, ..., mn) and after Conjecture 3.9.3 as the analogous question for a (-n)-curve with n > 1. ([math.colostate.edu](https://www.math.colostate.edu/~miranda/preprints/RecentDevelopments6_12.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper's actual target: it compares nonemptiness of a plane interpolation system for n generic points with the nonemptiness of the corresponding system in which the first r points are forced to lie on one line and the remaining points are otherwise general; it also captures that the comparison is made under a degree bound involving m1 + ... + mr. This is exactly the content-area of Problem 3.9.4. ([math.colostate.edu](https://www.math.colostate.edu/~miranda/preprints/RecentDevelopments6_12.pdf))
missing_details: The exact target is Problem 3.9.4, not Conjecture 3.9.3 itself; Problem 3.9.4 is posed as the analogous question after Conjecture 3.9.3. ([math.colostate.edu](https://www.math.colostate.edu/~miranda/preprints/RecentDevelopments6_12.pdf))

The paper uses the strict hypothesis d > m1 + ... + mr, not d >= m1 + ... + mr. This is the main substantive discrepancy in your draft. ([math.colostate.edu](https://www.math.colostate.edu/~miranda/preprints/RecentDevelopments6_12.pdf))

The ambient setting should be stated explicitly as the projective plane P^2, and L(d | m1, ..., mn) is introduced as the linear system of homogeneous polynomials of degree d through n generic points with multiplicities at least m1, ..., mn. ([math.colostate.edu](https://www.math.colostate.edu/~miranda/preprints/RecentDevelopments6_12.pdf))

The two configurations should be distinguished more sharply: in the first system all n base points are generic; in the second, the first r points are collinear and the n points are otherwise general. ([math.colostate.edu](https://www.math.colostate.edu/~miranda/preprints/RecentDevelopments6_12.pdf))

A stand-alone version should quantify the parameters: integers n and r with 1 <= r <= n, degree d, and multiplicities m1, ..., mn. Section 3.9 leaves these positivity/integrality conventions implicit in the interpolation notation, so they should be made explicit in the rewrite. ([math.colostate.edu](https://www.math.colostate.edu/~miranda/preprints/RecentDevelopments6_12.pdf))

Your notation overloads L(d; ...) for two different point configurations; the refined version should define the generic-point system and the partially collinear system separately to avoid ambiguity. ([math.colostate.edu](https://www.math.colostate.edu/~miranda/preprints/RecentDevelopments6_12.pdf))

It helps to spell out that 'nonempty' means there exists a nonzero homogeneous degree-d plane polynomial (equivalently, a plane curve of degree d) satisfying the prescribed multiplicity conditions. This is the meaning of the linear-system notation used in Section 3.9. ([math.colostate.edu](https://www.math.colostate.edu/~miranda/preprints/RecentDevelopments6_12.pdf))

The nearby discussion adds an important scope restriction: some genericity hypothesis is essential, and the authors give counterexamples if one allows more complicated special-position configurations (for example, several lines carrying many points). That context should not be built into the formal question, but it is part of the paper-faithful scope. ([math.colostate.edu](https://www.math.colostate.edu/~miranda/preprints/RecentDevelopments6_12.pdf))

Section 3.9 does not add a separate characteristic or field hypothesis in the local statement, so a faithful rewrite should not introduce extra assumptions beyond the projective-plane interpolation setting unless explicitly labeled as editorial clarification. ([math.colostate.edu](https://www.math.colostate.edu/~miranda/preprints/RecentDevelopments6_12.pdf))
refined_question: In the projective plane P^2, let L(d | m1, ..., mn) denote the linear system of homogeneous polynomials of degree d passing through n generic points with multiplicities at least m1, ..., mn. Let L_col(d | m1, ..., mr; m_{r+1}, ..., mn) denote the analogous linear system in which the first r base points are collinear and the n points are otherwise general. For integers 1 <= r <= n, is it true that whenever d > m1 + ... + mr, the system L(d | m1, ..., mn) is nonempty if and only if L_col(d | m1, ..., mr; m_{r+1}, ..., mn) is nonempty? ([math.colostate.edu](https://www.math.colostate.edu/~miranda/preprints/RecentDevelopments6_12.pdf))
justification: The draft is aimed at Section 3.9, not at the introduction's Conjecture 1.1 / Proposition 1.2 / Theorem 1.3: the paper first defines L(d | m1, ..., mn) for generic points, then introduces the variant with the first r points collinear, and immediately states Problem 3.9.4 asking exactly whether nonemptiness is preserved under that degeneration, provided d > m1 + ... + mr. The paper also says this question arose as an analogue of Conjecture 3.9.3 for a (-n)-curve with n > 1 and notes that, if true, it would simplify induction arguments toward SHGH; it further warns that a genericity condition is essential by giving multi-line counterexamples. Since the paper does not state an explicitly proved equivalent reformulation of Problem 3.9.4, no alternate equivalent formulation should be supplied. ([math.colostate.edu](https://www.math.colostate.edu/~miranda/preprints/RecentDevelopments6_12.pdf))
